result.topic_en: Riemann reduces the quadratic form $(a\,d\alpha+c\,d\gamma)^2+2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta$, by substitutions of variables, to normal forms and distinguishes three cases according to whether $\varphi(\beta)$ and $\psi(\alpha)$ vanish, aiming at curves of constant temperature (isotherms) in heat conduction.
result.transcription:
Ex aequatione (12) sequitur $c\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}-a\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}$ et proinde $\frac{\partial \frac{a}{c}}{\partial\beta}$ a $\gamma$ [-non-] pendere {+non+} posse. Si itaque {+ponimus+} [-$a=$-] $a=a_1+\gamma a_2$
sequitur $a_2$ esse formae $c\,f(\alpha)$ et $f(\alpha)$ a $\beta$ independens. Habemus itaque:
$(a\,d\alpha+c\,d\gamma)^2+2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta=(a_1\,d\alpha+c(f(\alpha)\,d\alpha+d\gamma))^2+2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta$.
Introducendo igitur {+loco+} $\gamma$ novam variabilem $\gamma+\int f(\alpha)d\alpha$ efficitur ut $a$ a $\gamma$ non pendeat. Quo pacto aequatio (13)
formam hanc induit:
$m\frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial\alpha^2}-\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial m}{\partial\alpha}=0$ \qquad $\frac{a}{c}+\gamma\frac{\partial c}{c}$
quae aequatio simul cum aequatione (11) hasce praebent:
$\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}}{\partial\alpha}=\frac{\partial\log m}{\partial\alpha}$ \qquad $\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial\log m}{\partial\beta}$ \qquad $c^2d\gamma^2+\frac{2}{\psi\alpha}\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}d\beta\,d\beta$
e quibus sequitur:
$\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}=m\,\varphi(\beta)$ \qquad $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}=m\,\psi(\alpha)$
Nunc distinguendi sunt tres casus:
1° si $\varphi(\beta)=\psi(\alpha)=0$ habetur $c=$ const. ac proinde ex aequatione (12) $\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}=0$; itaque introducendo loco $\gamma$ novam
variabilem $c\gamma+\int a\,d\alpha$ efficitur [-ut-] $a$ fiat $=0$ $c=1$. Tunc ex [-$\gamma$-] aequatione (13), quae sola [-non-] manet sequitur
$\frac{\partial^2\log m}{\partial\alpha\,\partial\beta}=0$ unde: $m=\chi(\alpha)\,\chi_1(\beta)$. Introducendo itaque loco $\alpha$ $\beta$ novas variabiles $\int\chi\alpha\,d\alpha$, $\int\chi_1\beta\,d\beta$ forma
nostra in hanc transit:
$d\gamma^2+2\,d\alpha\,d\beta$
Quae substituto $\alpha=x+iy$ $\beta=x-iy$ $\gamma=z$ praebet: $dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$. Curvae itaque $\alpha=$ const $\beta=$ const
in quibus temperatura $u$ est constans in hoc casu {+sunt+} lineae rectae parallelae.
2° si $\varphi(\beta)=0$ $\psi(\alpha)$ non $=0$ $c$ a $\alpha$ independens evadit. et e (12) sequitur $\frac{\partial}{\partial\beta}\frac{a}{c}$ a $\beta$ pendere non posse.
Tum simili modo ut supra efficitur [-ut-] $a$ sit $=0$ et porro habetur $m=\frac{1}{\psi(\alpha)}\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}$ quo pacto omnibus
aequationibus (11)...(12) satisfactum est. Introductis novis variabilibus pro $\alpha$ et $\beta$: $\int\frac{d\alpha}{\psi\alpha}$, $c$ habemus
formam: $\beta^2d\gamma^2+d\alpha\,d\beta$, quae in formam $dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$ transit, posito: \qquad $\left\{m\frac{\partial^2 m}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial m}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial m}{\partial\beta}\right.$
$x+iy=\alpha$ \quad $x-iy=\beta-\alpha\gamma^2$ \quad $z=\alpha\gamma$
at hae aequationes curvas reales $\alpha=$ const. $\beta=$ const. praebere nullo modo possunt.
Casus $\psi(\alpha)=0$ $\varphi(\beta)$ non $=0$ ab hoc essentialiter non differt.
3° Si neque $\varphi(\beta)$ neque $\psi(\alpha)$ evanescit effici potest introductis novis variabilibus $\int\frac{d\alpha}{\psi(\alpha)}$ $\int\frac{d\beta}{\varphi(\beta)}$ pro $\alpha$ et $\beta$
ut fiat:
$\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}=m$ \quad $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}=m$ \quad $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}-\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}=0$
quae aequationes praebent:
$c=f(\alpha+\beta)$ \quad $m=f'(\alpha+\beta)$
Tum sequitur ex aequatione (13)
$\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial ac}{\partial\beta}}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial\log cm}{\partial\beta}$
[-$\pm$-] unde habetur.
$ac=f^2\varphi(\alpha)+\psi(\alpha)$
[Randnotizen: $c(\varphi\alpha\,d\alpha+d\gamma)+\frac{\psi\alpha}{c}d\alpha$ \quad $c\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}-a\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}=0$ \quad $a\,d\alpha+c\,d\gamma$ \quad $c(\frac{a}{c}d\alpha+d\gamma)$ \quad $\gamma+\int\frac{a}{c}d\alpha$ \quad $\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial m}{\partial\alpha}}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial\log m}{\partial\alpha}$ \quad $\frac{\partial\log m}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}}{\partial\beta}$ \quad $\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial m}{\partial\beta}}{\partial\alpha}=\frac{\partial\log m}{\partial\alpha}$ \quad $\frac{1}{m}\frac{\partial m}{\partial\beta}=f(\beta)$ \quad $\frac{\partial\log m}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial\log ff'}{\partial\beta}$ \quad $c\frac{\partial ac}{\partial\beta}=\log cm+\psi(\alpha)$ \quad $\frac{\partial ac}{\partial\beta}=cm\,\varphi(\alpha)+$]
Nunc introducendo loco $\gamma$ variabilem $\gamma+\int\varphi(\alpha)d\alpha$ efficitur, ut $\varphi(\alpha)=0$ evadat ac proinde $ac=\psi(\alpha)$
Deinde e (12) habemus: $f''+\frac{\psi(\alpha)^2}{f^3}f'=0$ \quad $\frac{f''f^3}{f'}=-\psi\alpha^2$. Quum pars altera hujus aequationis a sola
variabili $\alpha$, pars altera ab $(\alpha+\beta)$ pendeat [-nec-] patet alteram utram constanti $+k^2$ aequari debere, quo
pacto ad determinandam functionem $f$ aequationem differentialem secundi gradus obtinemus:
$f''-\frac{k^2f'}{f^3}=0$
Quibus omnibus rite perpensis [-e-] aequationibus (11)...(12) satisfieri facile perspicitur. At integrando hanc
aequationem prodit: $2f'=k_1^2-\frac{k^2}{f^2}$ designando $k_1$ [-novam-] [-nov-] constantem.
[-Nunc-] si facimus $\alpha=x+iy$ $\beta=x-iy$ et loco variabilis $\gamma$ novam variabilem [-$\gamma+ik\int\frac{d\alpha}{f\alpha}$-] $\gamma-ik\int\frac{d\alpha}{f^2}$
obtinemus:
$(c\,d\gamma+a\,d\alpha)^2+2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta=(f\,d\gamma+\frac{k}{f}d\gamma)^2+2f'(dx^2+dy^2)=f^2d\gamma^2+2a\,d\gamma\,dy+2f'dx^2+k_1^2dy^2$
Sed posito:
$2f'dx^2=2\frac{df^2}{f'}=\frac{4f^2df^2}{f^2k_1^2-k^2}=d\xi^2$
fit: \quad $d\xi=\frac{2f\,df}{\sqrt{f^2k_1^2-k^2}}$ \quad $\xi=\frac{2}{k_1^2}\sqrt{f^2k_1^2-k^2}$ \quad $\frac{k_1^4}{4}\xi^2=f^2k_1^2-k^2$ \quad $f^2=\frac{k^2}{k_1^2}+\frac{k_1^2}{4}\xi^2$

methods.what: Removing the $\gamma$-dependence of $a$ by substituting a new variable
methods.quote: Introducendo igitur {+loco+} $\gamma$ novam variabilem $\gamma+\int f(\alpha)d\alpha$ efficitur ut $a$ a $\gamma$ non pendeat.

methods.what: Derivatives of $c$ expressed through $m$ and arbitrary functions
Case 1: separation of $\log m$ and reduction to the Euclidean metric
Case 1: complex substitution giving the flat metric
Case 2: substitution that turns $\beta^2d\gamma^2+d\alpha\,d\beta$ into the Euclidean form
Separation-of-variables argument yielding an ODE for $f$
Change of variable $\xi$ and expression of $f^2$

items.quote:
Curvae itaque $\alpha=$ const $\beta=$ const
in quibus temperatura $u$ est constans in hoc casu {+sunt+} lineae rectae parallelae.
items.english: Hence the curves $\alpha=$ const, $\beta=$ const, on which the temperature $u$ is constant, are in this case parallel straight lines.

items.quote: at hae aequationes curvas reales $\alpha=$ const. $\beta=$ const. praebere nullo modo possunt.
items.english: But these equations can in no way give real curves $\alpha=$ const., $\beta=$ const.

items.quote: Casus $\psi(\alpha)=0$ $\varphi(\beta)$ non $=0$ ab hoc essentialiter non differt.
items.english: The case $\psi(\alpha)=0$, $\varphi(\beta)$ not $=0$ does not differ essentially from this one.

items.quote: Quibus omnibus rite perpensis [-e-] aequationibus (11)...(12) satisfieri facile perspicitur.
items.english: With all this duly considered, it is easily seen that equations (11)...(12) are satisfied.
